[h1]Patch 1.8.2.0 is now live![/h1] 

Hey everyone,
with this update we added our own friend system to the game. This has one main advantage: You can now more easily play with your friends across devices and platforms. It will also allow us to design more gameplay features around the friend system in the future to provide a bit more depth to the game.
This change also means that we are moving away from the Steam friendlist. Some of you probably won't be too thrilled about having to manually add the friends you've been playing with in the past to the new friendlist. That's why we've tried to make this transition a little smoother and show you suggested friends. These are friends from your Steam friends list who also own Scribble It!.
We are slowly but surely bringing the game to more and more devices and platforms. This means that some of our old systems have to be replaced by new ones. This is also the reason we added dedicated servers in the past and will continue to make everything cross-platform in the future. We hope you understand that we want to bring the game to as many players around the world as possible and therefore need to be as platform agnostic as possible.


As always, we encourage every one of you to give us feedback or opinions about the game on our [url=discord.gg/scribbleit]Discord[/url] or on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

[h1]Patch 1.7.6.0 is now live![/h1] 

We updated the game once again and this is what we changed:

[h2]Chat Redesign & New Emote[/h2]
A new emote has been added. We felt like giving other players a "Thumbs Up" from time to time would improve the ability to express your feelings :) 👍🏻
Also the chat has been changed. You can now permanently see the chat once you click on the new expand button that is attached to the toolbar. We also added indicators for players that guessed correct. This should make it easier to see who you're chatting with!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/0a17c3d3747d817aaf9245b8f17ac7034c8eb8ee.gif[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
Other than that some lobby settings have been changed. We removed the settings to disable tools and change the max guess amounts. We saw that these settings we nearly never used. In the future, we're more likely to release entire game modes that take these setting options and turn them into more exciting gameplay than the settings have allowed so far. 
The update also fixes a bug in our art contest. The winners of the last contest are now correctly shown in the art contest tab. All winning artworks will be shown a bit longer to make up for the lost time due to the bug. 

Also, the Brands word package had to be removed to avoid legal issues.

[h2][b]Important information:[/b] [/h2]
With the next patch we will improve the state of handling languages. There will no longer be a distinction between UI and in-game language. All languages that are available will cover the entire game. This will allow us do develop the game much faster and get rid of lots of ugly restrictions, edge cases  and special treatments that are currently present in the game. [b]This means that some smaller languages will no longer be available BUT WE WILL CONTINUE TO ADD NEW LANGUAGES AS FAST AS POSSIBLE[/b] and we understand that some of you may be unhappy with this. Right now, this is the only way for us to move forward. If you would like to help translating the game into your language, please message us on Discord or visit the [url=https://crowdin.com/project/scribble-it]Crowdin project[/url].


As always, we encourage every one of you to give us feedback or opinions about the game on our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/Yx4nyam]Discord[/url] or on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

notes.title: Patch 1.6.0 Notes
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/49ff76c0274e01b895b510756c00b3375801c1a8.png[/img]

[h1]Patch 1.6.0 ist jetzt live![/h1]
Es ist eine Weile her, seit wir einen größeren Patch für das Spiel veröffentlicht haben, aber wir waren in der Zwischenzeit nicht untätig. Dieses Update bringt eine Reihe von Änderungen mit sich. Eine kurze Zusammenfassung: Ihr könnt jetzt (mit Respekt) Emojis spammen, es gibt rotierende Spielmodi, euer Lieblingsavatar ist jetzt viel größer, ihr verdient beim Spielen Trophäen für gute Leistungen und öffentliche Spiele zu finden, ist jetzt viel einfacher. Schauen wir uns die Änderungen genauer an!

[h2]Neues Emoji-System – Bye Bye, Chat[/h2]
Wir lieben es, frischen Wind in das bewährte Spielkonzept vom Malen und Raten zu bringen. Deshalb haben wir einige große Änderungen vorgenommen. Der Kern des Spiels bleibt unangetastet, aber einige UI-Elemente wurden überarbeitet.

[h3]Spieler-Anzeigen[/h3]
Die wichtigste Änderung: Wir verabschieden uns vom Chat-Fenster. Aber keine Sorge: Ihr könnt immer noch eure Stammbäume mit Fremden diskutieren – nur nicht mehr in Form eines typischen Chats. Übrigens: Das Stummschalten anderer Spieler ist jetzt viel einfacher! 
Ab sofort hat jeder Spieler seine eigene Spieler-Anzeige. Ihr könnt in Echtzeit sehen, was andere Spieler tippen und wann sie anfangen zu tippen. Knappe & richtige Antworten, Punktzahl, Platzierung und alles Wichtige findet ihr in und um eure Spieler-Anzeige. So sieht das Ganze aus:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/d3bc64a859427530c3e3bb27413d6eb8890fcd35.png[/img]

[h3]Emojis[/h3]
Um für eine emotionalere, aber dennoch inhaltsvolle und halbwegs zivilisierte Kommunikation zu sorgen, haben wir Emojis ins Spiel integriert. In den kommenden Monaten werden wir noch mehr Emojis hinzufügen, damit ihr immer genau zeigen könnt, was ihr fühlt – besonders dann, wenn wieder mal niemand errät, was ihr gezeichnet habt.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/235f463f3d3a223919d68f55518911f94035342e.gif[/img]

[h2]Schnelle Spiele[/h2]
Um die bisher mangelnde Masse an öffentlichen Spielen zu erhöhen, haben wir das Matchmaking überarbeitet. Es ist nicht mehr notwendig, öffentliche Lobbys manuell zu erstellen. Stattdessen könnt ihr einfach auf „Schnelles Spiel“ klicken, und die Suche nach einem Match beginnt. Sobald drei weitere Spieler gefunden wurden, werdet ihr einem [b]Guess It![/b]-Spiel zugewiesen. Der Wortpaket-Pool für diese Matches besteht aus allen offiziellen Wortpaketen, die zufällig ausgewählt werden.

Derzeit ist es nicht möglich, sich mit einer Gruppe von Freunden in diese Spiele einzureihen. Aber keine Sorge: Ihr könnt weiterhin private Lobbys erstellen, um mit euren Freunden zu spielen. Klickt dazu einfach auf den neuen Button „Mit Freunden spielen“ im Hauptmenü.

Mit diesen Änderungen möchten wir die Wartezeiten verkürzen, neuen Spielern einen besseren Einstieg bieten und Solospielern ein angenehmeres Erlebnis mit weniger Frust durch zufällige Host-Kicks oder Abstimmungen bieten.

[h2]Event-Spielmodi[/h2]
Ab heute führen wir rotierende Event-Spielmodi ein. In regelmäßigen Abständen werden neue Spielmodi zum Spiel hinzugefügt und im Hauptmenü präsentiert. Sie stehen allen Spielern zur Verfügung.
Der erste Event-Spielmodus ist ein alter Bekannter: Rate It!
Wir haben uns für Rate It! entschieden, da viele Spieler nie wirklich die Chance hatten, diesen Modus zu spielen, da er die Premium-Version und eine Gruppe von Freunden erforderte.
Wir haben das Bewertungssystem von Rate It! überarbeitet und hoffen, dass euch die neue Version genauso viel Spaß macht wie uns!

[h2]Punktesystem[/h2]
Apropos Punktesystem: Wir haben einige große Änderungen am Punktesystem unseres klassischen Spielmodus Guess It! vorgenommen.
Das alte System erlaubte eine sehr präzise Bewertung der Spielerleistung. Eure Punktzahl spiegelte wider, ob ihr nur einen Tick schneller wart als andere oder deutlich schneller. Allerdings empfanden wir es als wenig befriedigend oder motivierend, eine vier- bis fünfstellige Zahl steigen zu sehen. Zudem waren Punktzahlen von 5000+ manchmal schwer zu vergleichen.

Das neue System führt zwei neue Mechaniken ein: Medaillen 🏅 und Trophäen 🏆.
Durch Raten und Zeichnen verdient ihr verschiedene Medaillen. Am Ende einer Runde werden Medaillen in Trophäen umgewandelt. Der Spieler mit den meisten Trophäen gewinnt das Spiel.
Das Kernprinzip von Scribble It! bleibt jedoch bestehen: Schnell raten und gut zeichnen, um zu gewinnen!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/dbe98aa3fb5e9e52a7f4f6f34bdd2c66700304f6.gif[/img]

Wie immer freuen wir uns über euer Feedback und eure Meinungen zum Spiel – entweder auf unserem [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/Yx4nyam]Discord[/url] oder auf [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

[h3]Patch-Notes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Schnelles Spiel überarbeitet, öffentliche Spiele müssen nicht mehr manuell erstellt werden
[*] Schnelles Spiel-Suchen können jetzt nur noch für einen Spielmodus gleichzeitig gestartet werden
[*] Neuer Ladebildschirm mit Spieler-Vorschau hinzugefügt
[*] Rate It! als ersten rotierenden Spielmodus eingeführt
[*] Bewertung in Rate It! basiert nun auf Medaillen statt Zahlen
[*] Rate It! kann jetzt nur noch mit maximal 4 Spielern gespielt werden
[*] Guess It! (Schnelles Spiel) hat pro Runde ein statisches Wortpaket
[*] Spieler-Liste durch große Spieler-Anzeige ersetzt
[*] Chat durch Emojis / Sprechblasen ersetzt
[*] Punktesystem vereinfacht – Medaillen statt Punkte
[*] Spieler können laufenden Spielen nicht mehr beitreten
[*] Votekick in öffentlichen Spielen entfernt
[*] Simons Erklärungen entfernt
[*] Exhibition Wars! entfernt
[*] Teams entfernt
[*] Match-Ergebnisbildschirm kann jetzt verlassen werden, ohne auf den Host zu warten
[*] Free-Draw-UI überarbeitet für mehr Zeichenfläche
[/list]


[h3]Fehlerbehebungen[/h3]

[*] Problem behoben, bei dem der Store nicht immer öffnete, wenn auf Premium-Elemente geklickt wurde

[/list]

Hello everyone,
today's patch adds Ukranian UI to the game and fixes various bugs. Thanks to all of you who keep reporting minor (and sometimes major 😅) bugs and by doing this help us fix them!

We also added a Game Analytics system to the game. The reason for this is that the game is now at a point where the most requested and most necessary features have been added. Since Early Access entry in 2019 and official release in October, 2020 a LOT has changed. Visually and gameplay-wise the game has certainly grown. Now it is time for us to gain deeper insights into how our community actually plays the game. Often times in the past we had to guess what does and what does not work (short reminder of a certain patch, which was reverted very shortly after, that made it necessary for everyone in a lobby to have premium in order to play all game modes). Read more about which data we collect in our [url=https://detach-entertainment.com/privacy-policy]Privacy Policy[/url].

Qualitative feeedback in Discord, Reviews, comments and DMs always helps tremendously and will continue to be our most important way of connecting with you, our community. However, sometimes to make the correct decisions you need hard data and that is exactly what we hope to achieve with this change. Information for example about which tools are used the most and what lobby settings are popular will help us build upon the good things and make it easier to decide which things to cut from the game. 

Please rest assured that we will NEVER sell any of your data and handle it with the most care. If you have any questions about this integration of Game Analytics don't hesitate and reach out to our Devs in [url=https://discord.com/invite/Yx4nyam]Discord[/url].


As always, we encourage you to give us feedback or opinions about the game on our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/Yx4nyam]Discord server[/url] or on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/ecec893feabaca331d119c2a9fa02131f27961fa.png[/img]

[h1]Patch 1.4.0.0 is now live[/h1]

It's been a while! But we have not been lazy since the last update. Today several big changes are coming to the game. Let's dive into what exactly changed. 

As always we encourage you to give us feedback or opinions about the game on our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/Yx4nyam]Discord server[/url] or on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

Also we are now on [url=https://instagram.com/scribbleitgame]Instagram [/url]ːsteamhappyː


[h2]Report Player System[/h2]
Likely [b]the[/b] most requested feature. Now it is finally here: From now on you if you encounter offensive, negative, or disruptive experiences you can report players via an integrated report system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/fe565582c49969e94aaf24a98fa832199d1946a4.png[/img]

In the above screenshot you can see the reasons for reporting a player. Cases where a player receives a certain amount of reports will be reviewed by us and [b]sanctions [/b]against this player[b] will be put in place[/b].

[h3]Guidelines for reporting Players[/h3]

[b]Behaviour that you should report:[/b]
[list]
[*] Trying to game the system by writing letters on the canvas to tell others players the correct solution to a word.
[*] Drawing inappropriate or offensive things.
[*] Absolutely any kind of hate speech or racism.
[*] Spamming (i.e. writing the same thing or really long paragraphs over and over again). Note: Trying to guess the word and submitting many different guesses is [b]NOT [/b]spamming.
[*] Offensive player names.
[/list]

[b]Behaviour that you should NOT report:[/b]
[list]
[*] Strong language that does not insult or demean other people.
[*] Drawing poorly but still trying.
[*] Drawing really good.
[/list]

[b]Abuse of the report system will also result in sanctions.[/b]

[h2]New Lobby and Pause Menu UI[/h2]

We are slowly but surely bringing a new, more timely UI look and feel to the game. The first step in this direction is the introduction of a new sidebar. [b]Pressing Escape[/b] while inside a lobby or a game round will from now on open the sidebar. This allows you to easily access[b] lobby settings and a player list[/b]. Here is a short preview on what the new UI looks like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/6a010f749e6730330c06e74092224583f8147dd9.gif[/img]

You can also quickly access the playerlist menu by clicking on a player in-game or in the lobby. This means if you want to mute/votekick/report or simply have a look at a player's Steam profile you can do so very quickly by clicking on said player in the player list or in the lobby. The video below shows how this works.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/da13dfe33233204a389c2a77471fbd3b36c88632.gif[/img]

[h2]Improved Scoring System[/h2]
We continue to make changes to the way you earn points in Scribble It! based on your feedback.
With the new system a guessing player can earn a maximum of 1000 points and a drawing player can earn a maximum of 1250.
Our goal is to reward drawing skills and make the scoring fair for both drawing and guessing players. In big lobbies it is really hard to have everyone make the correct guess. This means if a player is so good at drawing that a full lobby guesses the correct solution he should be rewarded accordingly. In small lobbies it is more essential that players guess fast because convincing 3 players is a lot easier than 15 but here time should be of the essence.


[h2]Various other Changes[/h2]

Good news for all free-to-play players. We know that our yellow can sometimes strain the eyes a bit. Therefore we unlocked another green-ish color for all players.

Another change we made concerns the creation of word packages. You now have to accept our Word Package Guidelines everytime you are creating a new package. This is another measure to reduce the amount of obscene word packages that are being released into the wild.

Also we are happy to announce that we added Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Ukranian and Korean word packages.


Here is the full list of changes:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/756f5288cd28601a920e1341ab7e66bfce2aa971.jpg[/img]


[h1]Patch 1.2.0 is now live![/h1]

This patch contains improvements and new features from a variety of domains.
The complete list of changes can be found at the bottom of this post.
Let's dive into the most important changes of this patch:

[h2]Toolbar[/h2]

We changed some important aspects of our beloved toolbar.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/b29f67e722c5f4dde8b02f64623cb09f0fbbd5fc.png[/img]

Until now you could select between three different sizes of the same brush. We changed this to a single brush. Having only a single brush and changing its size with the scrollbar should be a much more intuitive and easy way to change the brush size.

As you can see [b]filled shapes [/b] made a comeback. We had these a while back but removed them. By popular demand from the community we added them back to the toolbar!

We also changed the color palette. We removed some colors and added some others. We also finally found some bugs that were causing problems when selecting the color resulting in the player having to click multiple times to change the color.

Now you might ask yourself...wait, where is the color wheel? Fear not it is still there. 
We wanted to make accessing the most important tools faster. The color palette surely is very important in a drawing game. While the color wheel allows for a more individual selection of colors it is most often used when there is more time at hand. This is why you can now switch between the two like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/ea0f331ee5b842d4acb63a8d6039fd8f925683d8.gif[/img]


You can see we also added another feature that has been lost but not forgotten....[b]welcome back opacity[/b]! We would love to hear feedback regarding this change from you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/f5cb089bce6488ada9b9912ed538b8dea227110c.gif[/img]

But not only that, we also simplified using shapes. Not using any modifier keys will now result in a simple upright shape. For the more experienced users we added an option to create [b]equilateral shapes[/b] as you can see in the animation above. You can change the key bindings for this in the options menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/5e6cb00278d1b1831a76dafbc2e4f9149d95a57f.jpg[/img]

[h2]Invite Codes[/h2]

Another much requested feature has been added to the game. From now on other players can join you via invite code. At the bottom of the player list you can now find a button which lets you copy the invite code. The  copy symbol can be clicked to copy the code without showing it in case you are a streamer and don't want to leak the code. You can also click on the text to see the actual code.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/48f0924796ec0e162c24f092534c09ed4776c4d7.jpg[/img]

To join a game via invite code simply go to the main menu, press "Play" and enter the code in the text field at bottom of the screen.

[h2]Game Mode Filter[/h2]

It is now possible to search for specific game modes. Enjoy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/dde2dc6012658f181edcb12d774d207e677c733d.jpg[/img]

[h2]Various Quality of Life Changes[/h2]

We implemented a way to hide the canvas buttons which are sometimes an annoying obstacle when drawing. The default binding for this is Shift+T but you can customize this in the options menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/59ce3c452085bc88a13d3772a7c82f987cd832cb.gif[/img]

We also added the option to hide the display of the current tool on top of the cursor when drawing. Another change we made is that the game now flashes in the task bar when an action is required. This should minimize the times you miss your turn in the future.

notes.title: A Message to our Community
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/2a52a300382aecd76e2ee31a50a4529f125e4c54.jpg[/img]

Dear community,

as most of you have noticed we changed the way premium lobbies work as part of the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1088150/announcements/detail/2921111055717228720]last patch[/url]. 
[b]Today we adjust these changes and go back to the old status.[/b] This means players who own the free-2-play version are once again able to play “Guess It! Grand Reveal” and “Rate It!” after a friend who owns the premium version invited them. We also went a bit further and now allow any player to find every game mode via quick search. Search options for specific game modes, as well as a lobby browser will follow soon.

Originally, after releasing Scribble It! in October 2020, the two game modes mentioned were only to be included in the premium edition. After our official launch we had some technical difficulties and were confronted with quite a few bugs. So, we decided it was fair to give our new F2P players the ability to test these premium game modes as a way to compensate for the poor gaming experience.

We communicated this state of the game and that it will change in the future via [url=https://discord.com/channels/653305619000066068/653313418333257739/769866221851770891]Discord[/url]. In hindsight this was not the correct way to handle this as many people simply did not see our statement regarding premium game modes. Lesson learnt. Rightfully, changing the state of premium lobbies back to the originally intended state as part of the patch on December, 6 caused a lot of irritation within our community. 

During the last days we read each and every one of your messages and listened to your concerns about how this change will impact the future. It became quite obvious that a lot of you love playing all of our game modes with their friends. We now understand that the changes we made were not at all aligned with our initial goal. With Scribble It! we wanted to create something that would take friends and those who might become friends out of their everyday lives for a short time and connect them through our game.

This is our very first game-release but that should not be an excuse for a poor decision on our end, [b]for that we apologize[/b]. 

Currently, we are two people that are developing this game part-time next to our main jobs.  We love creating games for you and want to spend as much time as possible doing exactly that which is why the premium edition exists. In the future we'd like to expand on new platforms and create more entertaining moments for our players. Without all of you this would not be possible therefore we want to thank you for the huge support since release. We have received enormous amounts of feedback from which we have learned A LOT.

We hope you will continue to accompany us on this journey.

- Zaratusa and soeanski, the developers

notes.title: Early Access Exit and the Future
notes.notes:
Hello guys,

more than one year has gone by since we published Scribble It! via the Steam Early Access program on the 26th of july 2019.

It sure has been a wonderful journey with ups, downs and everything in between. We are thankful for all the support we had and continue to have from you guys so thanks a lot! With the upcoming patch 1.0 we are officially[b] leaving Early Access[/b].  Looking back at the first playable versions of this game and [url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steam/apps/1088150/extras/roadmap.png?t=1598892769]all the things that have happened[/url] since last year sometimes feels a little unreal.

A whole lot of updates, some smaller some bigger, transformed the original ingame UI into what it is today. There is always room for improvement but we sure came a long way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/2cdd583a8519e8145db8c86041a33f8caa434a9b.png[/img]

But not only the way the game looks while playing it changed. Learning how to design accessible and intuitive UI elements is sometimes harder than it might seem and presented a major challenge for us. In July we completely overhauled the way of creating and updating a lobby and that was almost certainly not the last time we changed big UI elements :-P.

Hello everyone,

Also we entered the Steam Summer Sale with a 35% discount on the game!

From now on you can play with teams of up to 4 players. This is possible in all game modes. You do not have to create teams  which means playing solo like before is still possible. Any combination of team sizes from 1-4 can play against each other. Drawing together on a single scribble needs some practice and might be a tough challenge at first but that's what makes it fun!

Below you can see how teams look like in our lobby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/637300f4f06f959b9c50b86ee29b819932cc6579.png[/img]

We also changed the game creation menu. We separated the whole process into smaller steps and added breadcrumbs as a way to navigate through the process and visualize what is left. Below you can see what the new settings menu looks like. Changing a game setting is now a lot more intuitive, in case you do not understand a setting we added some toooltips to the different symbols and UI elements. We hope you like these changes as we put quite a lot of thought into the new menu. We would love to hear your feedback on it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/441c3fdae346fcf3e70cc84e049e058570af94ac.jpg[/img]


Another change we made concerns the naming of our game modes. From now on there are 4 game modes:
[list][*]In [b]Guess It![/b] one alternating Player illustrates a word - all other players have to guess! Time is everything as the quickest minds and the best artists will get the most points!
[*][b]Stream Wars![/b] works similar to Guess It!. However the viewers can help the streamer with guesses and also decide which word the streamer has to draw.
[*]In [b]Rate It![/b] All players illustrate the same word at once. Afterwards you have to rate the pictures of the other players - The perfect game mode to show off your drawing skills!
[*][b]Exhibition Wars![/b] is the streamers alternative to Rate It!. The players draw their pictures but only the stream viewers decide which picture looks best by giving their rating.[/list]

As you can see there is no more Scribble It! game mode as it was renamed to [b]Guess It! - Classic[/b]. The old Guess It! game mode is now called [b]Guess It! - Grand Reveal[/b]. This should make the names of our game modes and what they really are more memorable as both shapes of Guess It! are very alike and both are based on the classic pictionary game principles.

notes.title: DevBlog #2 Creating a Sharp UI with Distance Fields
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/272c36d4fe97688f0a89f455cbd06d5315feb67b.png[/img]

[b]Welcome back[/b] to the second issue of our Scribble It! Developers Blog. This time we explain our usage of [i]Signed Distance Fields[/i] as a method to make our UI razor sharp on almost any resolution.
Scribble It! is a 2-dimensional game. As such it is predestined to also run on machines with low-end hardware. Maybe someday even on a smartphone. 

Machines that have very old GPUs or even rely on onboard GPUs most often have a rather small texture memory. Yet modern games require the loading of a lot of big textures to make them visually appealing. To cope for that often times the player can reduce the texture quality in a settings menu - but that obviously makes the game look worse.

Using low resolution textures on 3D models to get a smooth gameplay might be a worthy tradeoff. But blurry 2D elements in the User Interface would seriously disturb the entire gameplay of Scribble It!. After all the game basically consists of only texts and UI elements.
We therefore needed a way to make the UI and text elements very sharp but without loading those big textures. Storing many high definition textures for all the different elements would mean high hardware requirements which is not somethin we wanted. There had to be a way to create sharp UI elements without using big textures.

We found the answer in a technique presented in a [url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/apps/valve/2007/SIGGRAPH2007_AlphaTestedMagnification.pdf]2007 Valve Corporation paper by Chris Green[/url] called „[i]Improved Alpha-Tested Magnification for Vector Textures and Special Effects[/i]“.
The presented usage of [i]Distance Fields[/i] allows you to create sharp images on many screen resolutions. These [i]Distance Fields[/i] make it possible to use small textures even for the highest resolutions. This way texture memory usage is being minimized and the game still looks good. Looking towards a possible mobile release for Scribble It! this was just what we needed.

This technique implicates that the resulting representation is „limited in terms of topology of features which can be represented“. Or to put it in other words: The approach is not feasible for really detailled and complex artwork. For Scribble It!'s rather simplistic approach to UI design this was not an issue.

We generated the [i]Distance Fields[/i] by using [url=https://github.com/Chlumsky/msdfgen][i]Chlumsky's Multi-channel signed distance field (MSDF) generator[/i][/url]. Below you can see an avatar in the form of paths and the resulting [i]MSDF [/i]texture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/669ef7877663d05b6c23b61139f045cc7c45b3f1.png[/img]

Afterwards we created a shader to render the final texture from the [i]MSDF[/i]. In this step the main challenge was to get smooth edges for every resolution. After testing out several different approaches to tackling this problem we found a solution that worked for us. We made the amount of smoothness that is applied to each pixel depended on the ratio of texture size and actual size of the render target.
The following material function is what we used to achieve that goal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/823dfc039b0bdc8dd9e088ba58ae3562eafb6ece.png[/img]

When generating a [i]MSDF [/i]we can set a value for [i]pxRange [/i]which represents the amount of surrounding pixels that will be included in the computation of the current output pixel. Specifically the [i]pxRange [/i]determines how much the [i]thickness [/i]parameter influences the final render.
Another parameter called [i]roughness [/i]is responsible for how smooth the edges will be and can be changed in the [i]MSDF [/i]material. This allows for a relatively comfortable adjustment of the different textures so they look good depending on their size and the type of artwork that they contain.

Below are some examples of what happens if the [i]roughness[/i] or [i]pxRange [/i]values are not correctly set. To make the different artifacts more visible we increased the [i]thickness [/i]of the depicted avatar a bit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35401706/2db0cf773fa0f31623c8ccf832c8b26579b76c16.png[/img]

Overall we are pleased with the way we were able to use [i]MSDFs [/i]to create sharp UI elements and texts. We had to make some adjustments to existing algorithms in our material and ultimately we are happy with the result. We hope you gained some insight into topic from todays issue of our DevBlog!

Marcel & Sören

Be sure to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!

notes.title: DevBlog #1 The Start of a Journey
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35401706/776d16bc6cd63a336a9575baa3766fb01584575b.png[/img]

[h1]The Start of a Journey[/h1]

The origin of every game lies in the birth of an idea.
Our idea was simple. [b]Bring the thrill of classroom drawing games back to life[/b] – but in a digital way. The idea was formed and molded almost exactly one year ago, on a lazy afternoon in the fourth story of a little office building right next to the Elbe river in Hamburg. 

Subject of this blog will be a developers view on how this idea resulted in our very first indie game release, what obstacles we met on the way and future problems that will problably rob our sleep.

In this very first edition we'd like to talk a bit more broadly on how we went about implementing the drawing system that is now a core part of the Scribble It! experience.
More details about what we did and the way drawing in UE4 can work will be laid out in future editions of this blog. Those will be published on a regular basis from now on.

[b]GPU vs. CPU[/b]

No matter what type of application, the first decision when implementing the functionality to let users draw is almost always the same: When to use GPU and when CPU?

Rendering user input to the screen via CPU often brings a lot of flexibility.
Implementing algorithms like [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood_fill]floodfill[/url] can be done without a lot of computational and programmatic effort. This allowed for an easy implementation of the Fill Tool that you know from Photoshop or other graphics editing tools in Scribble It!.  All the information about adjacent pixels is already there so you know which pixels to fill and which not.

When trying to do these things on the GPU you face the problem that shaders are executed on a per pixel basis. So you would have to go through multiple render passes to get the same information as on the CPU.
On the other hand GPU based rendering can result in a better performance. Especially when it comes to rendering a lot of textures. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35401706/b3ac9273def88e40c0f213a5fc8dfff2a83a25c1.png[/img]

[b]Flexibility vs. Performance[/b]

In Scribble It! we placed a lot of value on good performance. The drawing process had to be a fluent motion. Any delay between the mouse stroke of the user and the rendering of the respective pixels on the screen would simply make the gameplay feel bad. 

This is the reason that the rendering of brush strokes is handled on the GPU.
Every tick where the user is drawing we compute a starting point and in the next tick an end point based on the cursor position at first and second tick. In the next step this information is converted to a line that is then being painted according to current brush size and color.
On one hand this results in maximum performance but it also has a drawback: With our current way of handling things it is not possible to implement different types of brushes.

Enabling this feature would require us to use the classical approach that is used in many modern graphics editing tools: when drawing, along the drawn path a brush texture is rendered many times with a specific distance to the last texture. This technique is depicted in the picture below. 
A disadvantage of this classic approach is that the performance varies depending on the brush size and the distance between two brush textures, resulting in inconsistent performance and can cause stuttering. Bigger brushes and a smaller distance would implicate worse performance but it is necessary to have a small distance between brush textures to create perfect straight lines.

With our technique we have a constant performance because the shader is always applied to the whole canvas and therefore always takes the same amount of execution time. This way we can ensure that if a player's computer is able to draw a single small point on the canvas, it'll also be able to draw a line with the biggest brush size, which means we don't have to deal with any edge cases. As a result we have a smooth drawing experience.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35401706/b2e0f0cdac3ce6d40b402ec5e05e8ecee168a3bd.png[/img]

[b]Opacity[/b]

As we wanted to support drawing with different opacities we also had to make a little adaption to our technique. Drawing with opacities < 1 would result in different colors at start & end points  because the end point at every tick is the start point in the next tick. So the resulting color at that point would be too dark. 
We tackled this issue by creating a mask of the pixels that were to be filled and only then multiplied the current brush color with the mask. This way we got perfect opacity with a maximum of peformance. While the opacity feature did not make it into the current version of the game, it might make a comeback in the future.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35401706/d68972b107f9862d3f3d851e2004a210de2ba939.png[/img]

This technique prevents implementing something that is commonly called Flow. Flow means not filling the selected pixels immediately with respect to the opacity but fulling them depending on how long or how often they are being touched by the brush.
We decided against using Flow in Scribble It! to prevent the UI from being too cluttered with tools.

Anyway, this was a first broad overview of the underlying mechanisms that make drawing in Scribble It! possible. We hope you enjoyed the read and come back for the next edition in about two weeks.

Marcel & Sören    

Be  sure to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ScribbleItGame]Twitter[/url]!
